prompt:
A graph shows the variation with time t of the work done W by a mechanical hoist.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Work against time graph. Horizontal axis shows time t from 0 to 20 s. Vertical axis shows work done W from 0 to 50 kJ. A single straight line passes through the origin (0, 0) and the point (20 s, 40 kJ).]
What is the power output of the hoist?

answer.explanation: On a work-time graph, power is represented by the gradient: P = Delta W / Delta t = (40 * 10^3 J) / 20 s = 2000 W = 2.0 kW.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 is the inverse of the gradient: 20 / 40 = 0.50.
Option 2 is correct. P = gradient = 40 kJ / 20 s = 2.0 kW.
Option 3 reads the total work value at 20 s directly from the vertical axis without dividing by time.
Option 4 incorrectly multiplies work by time: 40 kJ * 20 s = 800 kJ s.
hints: Recall that power is the rate of doing work: P = W / t.
Determine what geometric feature of a W-t graph corresponds to W / t.
solution: Power is the gradient of a work-time graph. Gradient = (40 000 - 0) / (20 - 0) = 2000 W = 2.0 kW. Option B is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Identify that the gradient of a work against time graph is Delta W / Delta t = P.
Read points from the line: (0, 0) and (20 s, 40 000 J).
